newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT -JGBS SEEN SHRUGGING OFF IMF REPORT.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -JGBS SEEN SHRUGGING OFF IMF REPORT.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract is seen range-bound on Thursday, despite an International Monetary Fund (IMF) report saying it would likely be desirable for Japan to begin a credit tightening later in the year.
"JGBs did not fall significantly on LIFFE overnight despite the IMF's report, but it (the report) may make the September heavy on the upside today," said a trader for a city bank's securities unit.
But traders said JGBs are likely to receive a boost from a rise in U.S. Treasuries and a rise on LIFFE overnight.
The September ended at 126.55 on LIFFE overnight, up slightly from Wednesday's Tokyo close of 126.48.

The IMF's Executive Board said in its annual review of the Japanese economy released on Wednesday: "Directors believed that the current easy stance of monetary policy should be maintained for the time being, but that it would likely be desirable to begin tightening later in the year."
On Thursday, the market will focus on moves in Tokyo share prices and the degree of investor demand for cash bonds, traders said.
